summary: Concurrent retry window + timestamp normalization causing duplicate function-tool calls across SDKs
description:
Issue summary: Customer sees duplicate external tool/function invocations when clients retry requests during short retry windows. The duplicates only appear for multi-call chat interactions that include function/tool calling (webhook to downstream job system). Root cause suspected to be cross-SDK idempotency token normalization differences combined with a tight retry window and batching behaviors.

Impact: Several dozen duplicate downstream jobs were launched over a 48-hour window for a single workflow. Customer reports increased cost and a handful of duplicated side effects (emails, DB writes) requiring manual dedup. This impacts production traffic for NovusHealth's onboarding pipeline and is blocking confidence in enabling automatic retries.

Environment details: Production Redwood hosted API, region us-east-1. Customer uses three SDKs in orchestrator: Python 1.7.3 (requests-based), TypeScript 0.9.8 (fetch-based), and Go 0.6.2 (net/http). They run a multiplexer that batches small chat messages to improve throughput; server-side us-east serving fleet running redwood-serving v2026.02.3.

Observed behavior: When a transient 502 occurs in the API gateway, client SDKs retry (backoff) inside a 3s retry window. In several cases we observe two retries being accepted by the server as distinct requests (not deduped) even though the customer attached an idempotency token. Post-facto analysis shows the idempotency token value received by the backend differs between attempts in subtle ways (timestamp formatting and microsecond truncation). Some retries are routed to a different shard which has an older cached canonicalization rule.

Expected behavior: Retries with the same idempotency token should be deduplicated at server-side so that external function/tool/webhook calls are not executed more than once. SDKs should present a canonical idempotency header consistently across languages.

Attachments: sample headers and truncated logs are below in the logs field.

Customer asks: 1) immediate mitigation steps to stop duplicate downstream jobs; 2) guidance for SDKs and orchestration patterns to avoid duplicates; 3) whether we can make server-side idempotency tolerant to token formatting differences.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a chat session with two function calls in a single message batch (function A then function B).
Attach client-side generated idempotency token: iso8601 timestamp + nonce (e.g. 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456Z|nonce123).
Configure policy: client retries on 5xx with binary exponential backoff, max window 3s, max retries 2.
Simulate transient 502 on first request to trigger client retry.
Observe backend logs and downstream webhook logs for duplicated invocations of A and/or B.
logs: --- Request attempt 1 (from go): Idempotency-Token: 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123Z|nonce123 (go truncated microseconds)
--- Request attempt 1 (from ts): Idempotency-Token: 2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456+00:00|nonce123 (ts includes explicit timezone offset)

--- Server saw tokens normalized to different canonical strings on different shards: '2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456Z|nonce123' vs '2026-03-08T15:02:17.123Z|nonce123' vs '2026-03-08T15:02:17.123456+00:00|nonce123'
--- Downstream webhook invoked twice for function 'create_user_profile', request IDs: job-7791 and job-7792
comments: 2026-03-08 - Maya Chen (reporter): Initial ticket opened with sample logs and tenant details.
2026-03-08 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. Setting priority P2. Asking for SDK versions and whether the customer sets idempotency header manually or uses SDK auto-generation.

2026-03-09 - NovusHealth (CS contact - Javier Ruiz): We use SDK auto-generate in Python and TS; Go is a thin wrapper around the HTTP client with a small helper that formats timestamp via time.Format(time.RFC3339Nano) but then we locally trim trailing zeros for compactness. We did not think trimming would affect deduping.

2026-03-09 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed we can reproduce a mismatch locally by sending tokens with different timezone encodings and microsecond precision. Added a temporary server-side tolerance rule for this tenant to map tokens by parsed (timestamp, nonce) pair (accepted for 72 hours).

2026-03-10 - SRE (Anika Patel): Investigating shard config; observed a stale token-canonicalization lib on two older serving nodes. Raising an infra patch to standardize canonicalization across the fleet.

2026-03-11 - SDK PM (Ravi Singh): Proposing a patch across SDKs to normalize idempotency header generation to RFC3339Nano with forced 'Z' timezone and preserved microseconds; also adding tests and docs.
2026-03-12 - Support (Liam O'Connor): Customer accepted temporary tenant-level mitigation. Will schedule SDK updates and server-side normalization rollout. Marking ticket In Progress.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Clients produce semantically identical tokens but different string encodings; server-side shard-local canonicalization mismatch leads to treating them as distinct keys.

Hypothesis 2: Batching and multiplexing cause different attempts for the same logical request to be routed to different API gateway nodes which consult different token caches with different canonicalization behavior.

Findings: Reproduced locally using python/ts/go clients with deliberate token encoding differences. Found two serving nodes with redwood-serving v2026.01.7 missing the canonicalization patch. Once patched, deduping worked consistently in lab.
Risk: Until fleet-wide patch is deployed, customers using mixed-language orchestrators are at higher risk of duplicates under transient gateway errors.
resolution: Short-term mitigation (applied): Tenant-level request interceptor added that parses Idempotency-Token into (timestamp, nonce) and maps variants to a canonical token to dedupe for 72 hours. Customer confirmed duplicate jobs stopped after intervention.

Medium-term: Roll out redwood-serving patch v2026.03.15 that enforces server-side canonicalization of idempotency tokens by parsing timestamps and normalizing timezone+microseconds before keying. Will deploy to canary then fleet by 2026-03-15.

Long-term: SDK changes across Python/TS/Go to auto-generate tokens using a shared canonical format: RFC3339Nano with 'Z' suffix and fixed 6-digit microsecond field (pad/truncate to 6 digits). Add interop tests to SDK CI and include a migration note in the Idempotency section of the docs.

Docs/workflow guidance: Recommend customers include a stable nonce component (uuid4) and avoid ad-hoc string trimming. Add example helper functions for Python/TS/Go in docs page 'Idempotency tokens: best practices'

Follow-ups: Create INT ticket to track serving fleet rollout (INT-90123). Create GH PR for SDKs linked in related_github_prs. Postmortem to include cost impact analysis and recommendations for default tenant safety guardrails.
